item.text: I’ve got the core 2022 Ukraine diplomacy record now: Mexico helped draft humanitarian texts with France, backed UN condemnations of Russia’s invasion/annexation, and repeatedly called for dialogue while opposing punitive isolation that would close channels. I’m filling the gap with a few more official records so the final set stays balanced and not just one peace-proposal repeated in different wrappers.

item.text:
Chapter 2B is a limited-exposure case: Mexico had no international armed conflict in 2022, so the judgment space is mostly diplomacy, humanitarian response, and law-based positioning around the Russia-Ukraine war. The local prior shows zero internationalized conflict events and fatalities, so there is no Mexico-originating aggression to evaluate here.

**Reused Evidence**
- `REUSE_JSON: {"evidence_ids":["E0001"],"lenses":["2B.1","2B.7"]}`
  AMLO’s September 2022 peace proposal is still the clearest ruler-level peace initiative in the file.

- `REUSE_JSON: {"evidence_ids":["E0002"],"lenses":["2B.4","2B.7"]}`
  Mexico’s Zaporizhzhia security-perimeter call is relevant to civilian protection and de-escalation.

- `REUSE_JSON: {"evidence_ids":["E0003"],"lenses":["2B.4","2B.7"]}`
  Mexico’s warning about Zaporizhzhia’s humanitarian and environmental risk is another civilian-protection/de-escalation source.

**New Evidence**
- `SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Llamado del presidente Andrés Manuel López Obrador a la paz","publisher":"Presidencia de México","publication_date":"2022-04-09","url":"https://amlo.presidente.gob.mx/llamado-del-presidente-andres-manuel-lopez-obrador-a-la-paz/","claim":"AMLO sent a message to a forum focused on justice, non-intervention, peaceful settlement, and humanitarian aid for people affected by the war in Ukraine.","locator":"page title and snippet summary","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Direct presidential site with ruler-authored message and target-date context.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Direct 2022 ruler-period statement.","ruler_attribution":"Direct AMLO attribution.","contrary_evidence":["This is a public statement, not a demonstrated policy outcome.","It does not show operational leverage over the war."],"lenses":["2B.1","2B.6","2B.7"]}`
  This is the clearest direct AMLO statement in 2022 that ties Mexico to peace and non-intervention in the Ukraine war.

- `SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Mexico and US coordinate streamlined humanitarian assistance for Ukrainian migrants in Mexico","publisher":"Secretaría de Relaciones Exteriores, Gobierno de México","publication_date":"2022-04-21","url":"https://www.gob.mx/sre/prensa/mexico-and-us-coordinate-streamlined-humanitarian-assistance-for-ukrainian-migrants-in-mexico","claim":"Mexico and the United States coordinated to improve conditions for Ukrainian migrants in Mexico and to ensure orderly, safe, regular, humanitarian migration.","locator":"press release body and bullets","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Official foreign-ministry release with concrete humanitarian coordination measures.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Direct 2022 response to the Ukraine war.","ruler_attribution":"Indirect government attribution through Mexico's foreign policy and humanitarian response.","contrary_evidence":["This addresses war consequences rather than ending the war itself.","It does not show military restraint because Mexico was not a belligerent."],"lenses":["2B.4","2B.7","2B.10"]}`
  This is useful because it shows Mexico pairing peace rhetoric with concrete humanitarian handling of the war’s spillover.

- `SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Draft resolution /","publisher":"United Nations Digital Library","publication_date":"2022-02-25","url":"https://digitallibrary.un.org/record/3958806","claim":"Mexico is listed among the authors of the draft resolution on aggression by the Russian Federation against Ukraine in violation of the UN Charter.","locator":"Authors list and title record","source_type":"legal","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Primary UN document metadata identifying Mexico as co-author.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly within the 2022 emergency session on Ukraine.","ruler_attribution":"State-level attribution through Mexico's UN diplomacy; not personal military command.","contrary_evidence":["Co-sponsorship is diplomatic positioning, not operational enforcement.","It does not by itself prove success in reducing violence."],"lenses":["2B.1","2B.7","2B.10"]}`
  Mexico was aligned from the start with the UN move to condemn aggression and demand withdrawal.

- `SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Humanitarian consequences of the aggression against Ukraine : draft resolution","publisher":"United Nations Digital Library","publication_date":"2022-03-21","url":"https://digitallibrary.un.org/record/3965675?ln=en","claim":"Mexico is listed among the co-authors of the General Assembly draft resolution on the humanitarian consequences of the aggression against Ukraine.","locator":"Authors list and title record","source_type":"legal","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Primary UN document metadata identifying Mexico as co-author.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Direct 2022 fit and tightly tied to civilian protection in Ukraine.","ruler_attribution":"State-level attribution through Mexico's UN diplomacy.","contrary_evidence":["It is a draft-resolution record, not an implementation record.","It supports humanitarian posture more than demonstrated conflict resolution."],"lenses":["2B.4","2B.7","2B.10"]}`
  This is stronger than generic rhetoric because Mexico was an actual co-author of the humanitarian text.

- `SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Security Council Fails to Adopt Text Demanding Civilian Protection, Unhindered Humanitarian Access in Ukraine, as 13 Members Abstain","publisher":"United Nations","publication_date":"2022-03-23","url":"https://press.un.org/en/2022/sc14838.doc.htm","claim":"Mexico said it had negotiated a balanced humanitarian draft with France, abstained on the Russian draft because it lacked Article 2.4 and an unequivocal cessation of hostilities, and prioritized humanitarian action, civilian protection, and international humanitarian law.","locator":"Mexico intervention in the meeting record","source_type":"IGO","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Official UN meeting record with attributed national intervention.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Direct 2022 Security Council debate on Ukraine.","ruler_attribution":"Indirect state attribution through Mexico's UN mission and foreign ministry.","contrary_evidence":["Abstention can be read as cautious legalism rather than maximal pressure.","The record is diplomatic, not operational."],"lenses":["2B.1","2B.4","2B.6","2B.7"]}`
  This is one of the best pieces for showing Mexico trying to keep a humanitarian channel open while rejecting a text it saw as legally incomplete.

- `SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"General Assembly Adopts Text to Suspend Russian Federation from Human Rights Council, Continuing Emergency Special Session on Humanitarian Crisis in Ukraine","publisher":"United Nations","publication_date":"2022-04-07","url":"https://press.un.org/en/2022/ga12414.doc.htm","claim":"Mexico said it supported impartial investigations, the ICC and ICJ processes, and that even in war all channels should be maintained for dialogue with Russian authorities.","locator":"Mexico statement in the meeting record","source_type":"IGO","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Official UN meeting record with attributed Mexican statement.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Direct 2022 period fit and relevant to crisis diplomacy.","ruler_attribution":"Indirect state attribution through Mexico's UN delegation.","contrary_evidence":["Abstaining on suspension is a softer posture than maximal isolation.","It does not itself end or prevent the war."],"lenses":["2B.1","2B.6","2B.7","2B.9"]}`
  This is the clearest evidence that Mexico wanted accountability without closing negotiation channels.

- `SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"With 143 Votes in Favour, 5 Against, General Assembly Adopts Resolution Condemning Russian Federation’s Annexation of Four Eastern Ukraine Regions","publisher":"United Nations","publication_date":"2022-10-12","url":"https://press.un.org/en/2022/ga12458.doc.htm","claim":"Mexico said the occupied-territory referendums had no validity under international law, supported Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, supported Secretary-General-led diplomacy, and voted in favour of the resolution.","locator":"Mexico intervention in the meeting record","source_type":"IGO","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Official UN meeting record with attributed Mexican vote and explanation.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Direct 2022 fit and a major end-of-period Ukraine position.","ruler_attribution":"Indirect state attribution through Mexico's UN delegation.","contrary_evidence":["Voting for a resolution is not the same as stopping annexation or war.","This is still diplomatic/legal conduct, not battlefield conduct."],"lenses":["2B.1","2B.2","2B.7","2B.10"]}`
  This is the strongest late-2022 marker that Mexico stayed aligned with territorial integrity and anti-annexation norms.

- `SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Joint Statement of the Ministers of Foreign Affairs of Canada, Mexico and the United States","publisher":"Secretaría de Relaciones Exteriores, Gobierno de México","publication_date":"2022-06-10","url":"https://www.gob.mx/sre/prensa/joint-statement-of-the-ministers-of-foreign-affairs-of-canada-mexico-and-the-united-states?idiom=en","claim":"Canada, Mexico, and the United States reaffirmed support for Ukraine’s independence, sovereignty, and territorial integrity, condemned Russia’s invasion, called for humanitarian relief, and described a diplomatic path forward.","locator":"lines 64-68 of the page text","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Official trilateral statement with explicit text on Ukraine and diplomacy.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Direct 2022 fit with Mexico as a signing party.","ruler_attribution":"Government-level attribution through Mexico's foreign ministry.","contrary_evidence":["This is negotiated multilateral language, not a unilateral presidential order.","It shows alignment, not independent enforcement capacity."],"lenses":["2B.1","2B.4","2B.6","2B.7","2B.10"]}`
  This is useful corroboration because it is not just UN floor language; Mexico signed onto a North American diplomatic line.

**Search and Rejection Summary**
- I screened roughly 30 documents across UN press records, UN digital library records, Mexican presidential and foreign-ministry pages, Reuters/AP-style wire coverage, and local-language Mexican reporting.
- I kept 11 distinct URLs total in the chapter set, with most accepted items coming from primary or official diplomatic records.
- I rejected several near-duplicates of the same AMLO peace proposal, including wire writeups that only rephrased the presidential message.
- I rejected broad Ukraine explainers, general Russia-Ukraine background pieces, and non-Mexico-specific war coverage because they did not add ruler attribution.
- I rejected later 2023 follow-ups unless they were needed to clarify the 2022 posture; they were not, so they stayed out.
- I rejected domestic-Mexico security and social-policy material because it belongs to other chapters, not 2B.
- Some gob.mx and UN pages were inconsistent to open directly, but the search snippets were sufficient where I needed the precise claim.

**Remaining Gaps**
- There is still no direct evidence of private AMLO decision-making beyond public statements and Mexico’s diplomatic record.
- I did not find any credible evidence that Mexico initiated or prolonged a war, used proxies, or engaged in cross-border coercion in 2022.
- I also did not find a strong contrary record for 2B beyond Mexico’s cautious abstentions in some procedural votes, and those abstentions were framed as preserving dialogue and legal integrity rather than supporting aggression.
- More searching would likely return more of the same UN or SRE material, not materially stronger evidence.
